In Section II answer EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question (Section II: answer ALL questions, choosing one question from each pair of alternatives). For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define linear momentum. *[1 mark]*

(ii) State the principle of conservation of linear momentum. *[2 marks]*

(iii) Describe a real life situation in which this principle is applied. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Linear momentum** is the product of the mass of a body and its velocity: $p = mv$. It is a vector; its unit is $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ (or $\mathrm{N\,s}$).

(ii) **Principle of conservation of linear momentum:** when two or more bodies interact (collide or explode) and no external force acts on them, the total momentum of the bodies before the interaction equals their total momentum after it (in the same direction).

(iii) **Recoil of a gun:** before firing, the gun and bullet are at rest, so the total momentum is zero. When the gun is fired, the bullet gains momentum forwards; to keep the total momentum equal to zero, the gun gains an equal momentum in the opposite direction, so it recoils backwards. (Other examples: rocket propulsion, a collision between two vehicles.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A hunter fires a bullet of mass $0.05\,\mathrm{kg}$ with a velocity of $400\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ into a wooden block of mass $5\,\mathrm{kg}$ lying on a smooth surface. Calculate:

(i) the momentum of the bullet just as it hits the block. *[2 marks]*

(ii) the combined velocity of the bullet and the block given that they stick together on impact. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) $p = mv = 0.05\times 400 = 20\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$.

(ii) The block is initially at rest and the surface is smooth, so momentum is conserved:

$m_b u_b = (m_b + m_B)V$

$20 = (0.05 + 5)V = 5.05\,V$

$V = \dfrac{20}{5.05} = 3.96\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}} \approx 4.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In an experiment to determine the acceleration of a moving car, the magnitude of its velocity and the corresponding times were recorded over a period of $300$ seconds. The results are shown on the table below:

| Velocity / $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ | 0 | 4.0 | 7.0 | 8.0 | 10.6 | 12.6 | 17.0 | 21.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Time / $\mathrm{s}$ | 0 | 60 | 100 | 120 | 150 | 180 | 240 | 300 |

(i) Define velocity. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Plot a graph of velocity (y-axis) against time (x-axis). *[5 marks]*

(iii) Determine the slope of your graph and state its significance. *[3 marks]*

(iv) Use the graph to calculate the total displacement of the car. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Velocity** is the rate of change of displacement, that is, the displacement per unit time in a given direction: $v = \dfrac{\text{displacement}}{\text{time}}$ (a vector, in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$).

(ii) **Graph.** Draw the time axis (x) from $0$ to $300\,\mathrm{s}$ (for example $2\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $50\,\mathrm{s}$) and the velocity axis (y) from $0$ to $22\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (for example $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$). Label the axes with their quantities and units. Plot the eight points $(0,0)$, $(60, 4.0)$, $(100, 7.0)$, $(120, 8.0)$, $(150, 10.6)$, $(180, 12.6)$, $(240, 17.0)$, $(300, 21.0)$. The points lie close to a **straight line through the origin**; draw the best-fit straight line with a ruler (points evenly spread on both sides of it).

(iii) Take two points far apart on the line, for example $(0, 0)$ and $(300, 21)$:

slope $= \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{21 - 0}{300 - 0} = 0.07\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

**Significance:** the slope of a velocity-time graph is the **acceleration** of the car. The car moves with a constant (uniform) acceleration of about $0.07\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

(iv) The displacement is the **area under the velocity-time graph**. The area is a triangle:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2}\times\text{base}\times\text{height} = \dfrac{1}{2}\times 300\times 21 = 3150\,\mathrm{m}$ (about $3.1\times10^{3}\,\mathrm{m}$, that is about $3.2\,\mathrm{km}$).

(Adding the trapeziums between the plotted points gives $3145\,\mathrm{m}$, the same within reading errors.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define work. *[1 mark]*

(ii) State the principle of conservation of energy. *[2 marks]*

(iii) Describe the energy changes that take place when a stretched catapult projects a stone. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Work** is done when a force moves its point of application; it is the product of the force and the distance moved in the direction of the force: $W = F\times d$ (unit: joule, $\mathrm{J}$).

(ii) **Principle of conservation of energy:** energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form into another, so the total energy of an isolated system remains constant.

(iii) The stretched catapult (rubber band) stores **elastic potential energy**. When it is released, this energy is converted into the **kinetic energy** of the stone, which leaves the catapult with a speed. As the stone rises, its kinetic energy is converted into gravitational potential energy, and a little energy is lost as heat and sound.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A girl of mass $40\,\mathrm{kg}$ runs up a flight of stairs to the second floor of a building which is located $12\,\mathrm{m}$ above the ground floor, in $7.5\,\mathrm{s}$. Calculate:

(i) the work done by the girl to reach the second floor. *[2 marks]*

(ii) the power of the girl. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The work done against gravity equals the gain in potential energy:

$W = mgh = 40\times 10\times 12 = 4800\,\mathrm{J}$.

(ii) $P = \dfrac{W}{t} = \dfrac{4800}{7.5} = 640\,\mathrm{W}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In an experiment to determine the mechanical advantage of a certain machine, loads were applied to it and the corresponding efforts noted. The results are summarized on the table below:

| Load / $\mathrm{N}$ | 0 | 40 | 80 | 120 | 160 | 200 | 240 | 280 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Effort / $\mathrm{N}$ | 0 | 5.0 | 11.5 | 17 | 22.5 | 28.5 | 34 | 39.5 |

(i) Define mechanical advantage? *[1 mark]*

(ii) Plot a graph of load (y-axis) against the effort (x-axis). *[5 marks]*

(iii) Determine the slope of your graph and state its significance. *[3 marks]*

(iv) If the efficiency of the machine is $80\,\%$, calculate its velocity ratio. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Mechanical advantage** is the ratio of the load (output force) the machine overcomes to the effort (input force) applied to it: $\mathrm{MA} = \dfrac{\text{load}}{\text{effort}}$. It has no unit.

(ii) **Graph.** Effort on the x-axis from $0$ to $40\,\mathrm{N}$ (for example $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $5\,\mathrm{N}$) and load on the y-axis from $0$ to $280\,\mathrm{N}$ (for example $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ for $20\,\mathrm{N}$); label the axes with quantity and unit. Plot the points (effort, load): $(0,0)$, $(5.0, 40)$, $(11.5, 80)$, $(17, 120)$, $(22.5, 160)$, $(28.5, 200)$, $(34, 240)$, $(39.5, 280)$. They lie almost on a **straight line through the origin**; draw the best-fit line with a ruler.

(iii) Take two points on the line far apart, for example $(0, 0)$ and $(39.5, 280)$:

slope $= \dfrac{\Delta \text{load}}{\Delta \text{effort}} = \dfrac{280 - 0}{39.5 - 0} = 7.1$ (no unit).

**Significance:** the slope of the load-effort graph is the **mechanical advantage** of the machine ($\mathrm{MA} \approx 7.1$), which is constant for all the loads.

(iv) $\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{\mathrm{MA}}{\mathrm{VR}}\times 100\,\%$, so

$\mathrm{VR} = \dfrac{\mathrm{MA}}{\text{efficiency}} = \dfrac{7.1}{0.80} = 8.9$ (a value between $8.8$ and $8.9$ depending on the line drawn is acceptable).
